title: Best Shopify Developers (2026): Hire One for Your Store
description: How to hire a Shopify developer or store designer: what the package should cover, how to brief the job, price factors and red flags.
intro: A Shopify store can be live in days, but a store that actually sells needs clear product pages, a smooth checkout and correct settings for shipping, taxes and payments. Most problems come from a vague brief and from apps added without a plan. This guide shows you what to ask for.

faq.q: Do I need a developer, or can I set up Shopify myself?
faq.a: You can launch a simple store yourself with a free theme. A developer helps when you want a custom design, need to move from another platform, or have many products, variants or special features.

faq.q: Should the developer have access to my store?
faq.a: Give them staff or collaborator access, not your owner login. Keep the store, the payment settings and the domain in your own name, and remove their access once the job is done.

faq.q: Are theme and app costs included in the price?
faq.a: Usually not. Paid themes and apps are billed to the store owner, and many apps charge monthly. Ask the developer to list every paid theme and app they plan to use before you order.

faq.q: Can a developer move my store from another platform?
faq.a: Many do. Ask exactly what will be moved: products, images, customers, order history, blog posts and old page addresses. Redirects from old addresses help keep your search traffic.

faq.q: Who sets up taxes, shipping and legal pages?
faq.a: A developer can enter the settings, but the rules depend on where you sell. Decide the shipping rates and check your local tax and consumer rules yourself, or with an accountant.
